correctness.rationale: Scope is the q+1 F_q-linear lines in F_q², not every maximal isotropic additive subgroup in composite prime-power dimension. Each line is its own field symplectic perpendicular; for a Weyl label off the line the symplectic pairing runs through F_q, so the nontrivial trace character averages to zero. This yields the stated T_j eigenspaces and positive finite-time λ_j=x_j+(1−x_j)y with y=e^(−ct), including zero weights. Independently invert the generator in T_j−Id: its coefficient b_j must satisfy Σ_i b_i−b_j=g_j=−(d/dt)log λ_j on sector j. Summing gives Σ_i b_i=Σ_i g_i/q, and T_j−Id is the sum of the q−1 nonidentity Weyl conjugation differences divided by q. Hence γ_j=(Σ_i g_i−qg_j)/q². Nonnegative Weyl coefficients yield a GKLS generator; a negative one has a negative first-order Choi expectation along its orthogonal nonidentity Bell vector for a short propagator. Finite-time invertibility makes this propagator the unique intermediate map. In the simplex interior a least rate always corresponds to m=max_j a_j. Its exact expression is cyF(y)/[q²(1+my)], where F is the displayed root function. (Dividing by cyφ_y(m)/q² gives F/m, not F itself; the proof only uses the sign.) F(0)=A−qm and F(1)=q; F is nondecreasing, with strictly positive derivative unless all a_j=m. Thus A≥qm is necessary and sufficient, and A<qm gives exactly one crossing in (0,1) and local CP-indivisibility at every later time, with inclusive endpoint on the initial interval. At equality A=qm the leading term is c(qm²−Σ_j a_j²)y²/q², positive because all a_j>0 and not all equal. On a proper face with 2≤s≤q active weights, each active g_j<c(1−x_j) for t>0 and each absent g_j=c, so γ_k<0 in every absent direction; a vertex is the original semigroup. Substitution of qutrit weights (1/10,3/10,3/10,3/10) gives exactly y*=11/21. Inspected, did not run, the frozen finite numerical diagnostic. Its reported 182400 counts nonidentity-label units over the main test cases; the actual rate assertions there are made for one representative per direction, not 182400 distinct rate-to-formula comparisons. The continuous proof and all prime powers do not depend on that reporting convention.

evidence: Pointwise evaluation of (108) requires a time parameter and does not itself assert where in weight space sign holds for every time, or that an initially positive minimum never becomes positive again after a crossing.

The evaluated result uses the same minimizing index for every time and normalizes by that index's denominator, so each summand in F is monotone with derivative proportional to m−a_j. This proves single crossing and reduces the infinite-time test to the exact A−qm endpoint, including A=qm.
The previous prime-dimensional face examples and the MUB rate identity are explicitly excluded from standalone novelty credit.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact rate formula is strong input, but evaluating its least-rate sign over the entire trajectory requires a comparison and monotonicity argument, not just substituting d=q, recognizing a family alias, or taking the late-time necessary condition. The global result that this endpoint is sufficient and that failure has a unique permanent onset is the distinct structural claim.

evidence: A field-line span is a q-dimensional abelian diagonal algebra; the q−1 traceless directions of distinct line algebras are orthogonal. Their common eigenbases therefore form a complete set of mutually unbiased bases, since rank-one projectors in distinct algebras have trace overlap 1/q. The MUB pinchings are exactly these T_j.
Time rescaling makes the generalized Pauli decays e^(−dt) and e^(−ct) equivalent, and line coefficients and individual Weyl rates differ only by a positive normalization.
The similarly shaped Σ c_j≥d max c_j in the semigroup paper tests stationary semigroup spectra with a different meaning of c_j.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The finite-field parametrization is not a novelty argument by itself, because the same complete MUB pinching model covers it. A weight-only CP-divisibility test over all positive times is not a condition for time-homogeneity or for the mixed evolution to be a semigroup.

value.rationale: For a natural equal-rate mixture of mutually unbiased pinchings, a weight-only rule is useful in place of testing every time instance. The evaluated classification establishes a sharp distinction between immediate, delayed and absent loss of CP-divisibility, including a permanent-onset theorem and the critical tail behavior. The contribution is not the existing pointwise generator formula or a one-weight example; scope remains fixed weights, a common decay rate and the complete field-line family.
